notable_absence.finding: The page names three distinct internal permission strings gating three different actions - `cluster.analytics!manage` (expose a function from a library via CREATE ANALYTICS FUNCTION), `cluster.analytics!select` (execute an already-exposed function), and `cluster.admin.diag!write` (upload a library) - but only the third is tied to a named role ('normally only available to the role Full Administrator'). The other two are never mapped to any role in roles.md's 56-entry catalog on this page, so whether an administrator needs a role beyond Full Administrator, or whether these are Full-Administrator-implied permissions too, cannot be determined from this page alone.

cross_component_finding: This page is a rare case in the corpus where concrete Server-side permission strings appear directly in prose rather than as an abstract two-tier role/privilege claim - the registry's existing hasPrivilege record notes that Server's docs otherwise 'define a privilege tier, assert that roles correspond to system-defined privileges, and then never name a member of it' (all 55 roles.md permission tables use plain-English prose instead). Here, by contrast, three named permission strings appear verbatim (cluster.analytics!manage, cluster.analytics!select, cluster.admin.diag!write), which is a genuine counter-example worth flagging for reconciliation against that earlier finding - though it does not fully overturn it, since two of the three are still not tied to any named role (see notable_absence). Separately, the security section draws an explicit analogy to conventional database engines ('This is similar to an unfenced external function in a traditional RDBMS') to explain why Python UDFs run unsandboxed as the Analytics process's own user - a genuinely different security posture from js-udf's JavaScript UDFs, which this page does not compare against directly but which the round's framing flagged as worth checking.
cross_product_finding: No Capella-specific content appears on this page. The library-upload restriction to loopback-origin requests from an Analytics node is a Server on-premises administrative concept with no stated Capella analogue (Capella customers do not have node-level shell/loopback access at all).
